answer: Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes — coordination requires many low-weight votes that cancel each other out. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. The mechanism therefore aligns self-interest with network health: an attacker gains most by behaving honestly, because that is the only move that scales. Consider a dune as the anchor of the cost. A dawn stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a gale...
